Subject: FluxPay: p99 latency surge during peak — orchestration & customer comms

Hi team,

We're seeing a sustained p99 latency increase on gen-api for FluxPay beginning 09:02 PDT during their morning peak. Key signals:
- p50 ~ stable, p95 up ~30% -> p99 up ~220%
- overall throughput down ~18% for routes hitting long-context (>= 8k tokens)
- KV cache eviction events correlated with CPU pressure on node group 'rt-3'

PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-98234
Attached: p99-graphs.png

Immediate asks:
1) Ben: can infra apply the transient kernel-scheduling throttle on rt-3 and confirm rollback window?
2) Marissa/Product: confirm whether we should enable the conservative fallback model (smaller quantized variant) for FluxPay while we triage.
3) Evelyn/Sales: we need an interim customer note (ack + ETA) — suggest 60–90 minute window for mitigation.

I'll join an ad-hoc bridge in 10 mins. Priority: reduce customer impact while preserving token correctness.

— Soojin

Quick proposal while infra triages:
- Flip routing rule for FluxPay to route long-context requests to a conservative service pool (smaller batch sizing + tighter CPU cap). This is lower-risk than a full model swap.
- If that stabilizes p99 within 30m, we keep in place and plan a canary of the quantized fallback model during off-peak.

Ben: can you confirm whether we can apply the routing change via the runtime config (no code roll)? If so, we should avoid touching customer-facing model versions.

Evelyn: draft that short customer message (ack + we are applying protective routing) and I'll add the ETA.

— Marissa

On the bridge — quick technical notes:
- Observed kernel-scheduling contention on rt-3 caused by a small set of long-running decoder threads; those threads are coincident with requests that hit the 8k+ prefix window.
- I can apply a transient kernel-scheduler QOS throttle to rt-3 nodes now (no restart). That will prioritize short-lived tasks and should reclaim CPU for KV cache maintenance. Expect p99 improvement within ~8–12 minutes, rollbackable immediately.
- As a low-risk route, runtime routing switch (Marissa's idea) is preferred to a full model swap. I will prepare a fallback-config.diff that sets conservative batching and reduces max_tokens for the long-context route.

I'll push the throttle in 5 minutes and report back with graphs. Traces collected and saved to trace_dump.tgz.

— Ben
